lines.say: How does three hundred dollars of your own cash build credit?

lines.text: It matters: the CFPB estimated 7 million US adults had no credit record at all in December 2020.
lines.say: It matters: the C F P B estimated seven million US adults had no credit record at all in December twenty twenty.

lines.text: One way in is a secured card, where your deposit usually becomes your credit limit.
lines.say: One way in is a secured card, where your deposit usually becomes your credit limit.

lines.text: The issuer reports it to the credit bureaus like a regular card, and payment history is 35% of a FICO score.
lines.say: The issuer reports it to the credit bureaus like a regular card, and payment history is thirty-five percent of a FICO score.

lines.text: Our math: on a $300 limit, a $90 balance is 30% utilization, while $30 is just 10%.
lines.say: Our math: on a three hundred dollar limit, a ninety dollar balance is thirty percent utilization, while thirty dollars is just ten percent.

lines.text: Lower utilization is generally better, because the amounts you owe are another big slice of your score.
lines.say: Lower utilization is generally better, because the amounts you owe are another big slice of your score.

lines.text: To score you, FICO needs an account open at least 6 months and reported in the last 6 months.

lines.text: Later, some issuers let you graduate to a regular card, and timing varies. Leave in good standing, and the deposit comes back.

lines.text: Before you apply, check that the card reports to all 3 credit bureaus, because not every issuer does.

post.title: How a $300 deposit can turn into a credit history
post.ig:
How does $300 of your own cash build credit?
A secured card's deposit usually becomes its credit limit, and the issuer reports your payments to credit bureaus like a regular card.
Payment history is 35% of a FICO Score. Our math: a $90 balance on a $300 limit is 30% utilization; $30 is 10%.
FICO needs an account open at least 6 months and reported in the last 6 months. The CFPB estimated 7 million US adults had no credit record in December 2020.
Sources: CFPB (June 2025), myFICO, Federal Reserve (Dec 2024).
